summary: Independently reconstruct fixed-order recursive currents for bounded canonical admissible potentials in the book shifted cone, for a positive Hermitian background and2<=m<n. Four proofs give signed measure coefficients below degree m, a distributional top recursion, positive shifted wedges through top degree, and complete d/dc/ddc torsion identities. Each iterated limit is independent of approximations for its fixed order and agrees with continuous products when all potentials are continuous. No interchange of two bounded potentials or simultaneous decreasing convergence is asserted.

mathematical_checks: All pointwise weights use canonical bounded Borel representatives, not arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications.
Compactness of increasing smooth sublevel sets bounds all approximants by the potential norm plus one after a finite tail.
Gamma_m lies in Gamma_2; squared eigenvalues are bounded by the squared nonnegative trace, giving degree-one coefficient bounds.
Smooth shifted CLN estimates are established earlier and have no dependency on the new bounded recursion.
At each step only the order-zero current D_(p-1), with p-1<m, is multiplied by a bounded function.
Dominated convergence is against a fixed signed coefficient measure; moving lower factors are paired only after the outer potential is smooth and fixed.
Every raw-product term expands into q<m shifted admissible factors before the absolute-form coefficient bound is applied.
The q=0 smooth term is separate; for q>=1 the potential average has bounded sup norm, with no claim that its Hessian is uniformly bounded.
The top unwedged D_m is only distributional; no coefficient measure bound at degree m is used.
Subset expansions retain the inherited index ordering. Unused indices give constant limits.
Positive complementary tests append m-p nonnegative rank-one forms; Garding gives positivity of every shifted smooth wedge.
Positive-current trace bounds survive successive distributional limits, giving an order-zero Q_p and positive Radon Q_m.
Canonical bounded multiplication and local distributional differentiation give locality and fixed-order approximation independence.
For continuous potentials, Dini uniform convergence and the earlier uniform telescoping estimate identify the new wedges with continuous products.
The coefficient p-|I| counts first omissions and each omitted pair occurs twice; the minus sign from differentiating dc(omega) cancels its odd-degree interchange with d(omega).
Every torsion right-hand current has at most p-1<=m-1 potentials and hence measure coefficients.
With one bounded potential and smooth other factors, closed smooth multiplication commutes through the recursion; no two-bounded-factor commutation is inferred.
The source local unshifted ddcu cone is not silently replaced by the shifted omega+ddcu cone. The new proof expands smooth corrections explicitly.
